variants.name: ABCA4
variants.note: One copy of a harmful variant in ABCA4, a gene for the light-sensing cells of the eye. ABCA4 conditions, such as Stargardt disease (a cause of central vision loss), are recessive: they happen only when both copies of the gene carry a harmful variant. With one copy you are a carrier and usually have no symptoms. It matters for children if a partner also carries an ABCA4 variant.

variants.name: GAA c.-32-13T>G
variants.note: One copy of the most common variant behind late-onset Pompe disease, a slowly progressing muscle condition. Pompe disease is recessive, so one copy makes you a carrier, usually with no symptoms. It matters for children if a partner is also a carrier.
conditions: Glycogen storage disease due to acid maltase deficiency, late-onset

variants.name: GJB2 M34T
variants.note: One copy of a mild GJB2 hearing-loss variant. GJB2 hearing loss is recessive: people with two variants typically have mild to moderate hearing loss, and some have none. With one copy you are a carrier.

variants.name: GJB2 V37I
variants.note: One copy of a mild GJB2 hearing-loss variant that is common in people of East Asian ancestry. GJB2 hearing loss is recessive: people with two variants typically have mild to moderate hearing loss, and some have none. With one copy you are a carrier.
conditions: Knuckle pads, deafness AND leukonychia syndrome

variants.name: PMM2 R141H
variants.note: One copy of the most common variant behind PMM2-CDG, a rare inherited metabolic condition that appears in early childhood. It is recessive, so one copy makes you a carrier with no symptoms. Roughly 1 in 60 to 1 in 220 people of European ancestry carry it.

variants.name: VWF R854Q
variants.note: One copy of R854Q, the most common cause of type 2N von Willebrand disease, a mild bleeding disorder. Bleeding problems usually happen only with two copies, or together with another VWF variant; one copy usually causes none. Mention it to your doctor if you or relatives have unusual bleeding, or before surgery.
